Strong Consistency: Guarantees that all reads return the most recent write. It's like reading from a single, up-to-date source.
Bounded Staleness: Allows a slight delay between writes and reads, but with a defined maximum time lag. Data may not be immediately up-to-date but won't be too stale.
Consistent Prefix: Ensures that reads never see writes that occurred after they started. It provides a partial order of operations.
Eventual Consistency: No specific guarantees about when data will be consistent. Eventually, all replicas will catch up, but there's no fixed time frame.

A time-based retention policy stores blob data in a Write-Once, Read-Many (WORM) format for a specified interval. When a time-based retention policy is set, clients can create and read blobs, but can't modify or delete them. After the retention interval has expired, blobs can be deleted but not overwritten.
